titleText.en: Someday the 'in popular culture' section will have its own article with an 'in popular culture' section.  It will reference this title-text referencing it, and the blogosphere will implode.
titleText.noteEn: Unescaped quotation marks truncate the Spanish archive metadata after sección. The intended Spanish source continues: ‘En la cultura popular’ tendrá su propio artículo con una sección ‘En la cultura popular’. En él se hará referencia a este texto ALT, que hace referencia a él, y la blogosfera implosionará. The Spanish raster also changes the official first reference from episode 6, ‘Our Mrs. Reynolds,’ to episode 7, ‘Jaynestown.’ Both source images deliberately cut off the Battlestar Galactica bullet at the lower edge.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: tissue; a structural material in a living organism
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tejido can also mean woven fabric. In biology, it names a group of similar cells that form part of a plant or animal.

example.en: Plant tissue contains water.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here duro describes a material that resists pressure. In other contexts it can describe something difficult or someone acting harshly.

example.en: The ground is hard.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; helps encontrarse mean ‘to be found’ or ‘to be located’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With this use of encontrarse, se matches the thing being located: se encuentra for one thing and se encuentran for more than one.

example.en: The station is located nearby.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encuentra is the singular present form of encontrar. With the matching se before it, encontrarse can describe where something exists or is located.

example.es: El museo se encuentra en el centro.
example.en: The museum is located downtown.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Usado is usar's completed-action form. After a form of haber, it helps say that an action has happened; it does not change for gender in that construction.

example.en: We have used this tool.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: both; introduces the first of two linked items
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In tanto X como Y, tanto opens the first item and como introduces the second. The two items can be nouns, descriptions, or longer matching phrases.

example.es: Sirve tanto para estudiar como para descansar.
example.en: It is useful both for studying and for resting.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a noun, combustible is a substance burned to produce heat or energy. As a describing word, it can instead mean combustible or flammable.

example.en: The vehicle needs fuel.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here material names a physical substance used to make or build something, rather than a collection of equipment or supplies.

example.es: El vidrio es un material resistente.
example.en: Glass is a durable material.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’

example.en: I need a coffee cup.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: free; open for people to use or share
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Libre emphasizes freedom or lack of restriction. It is different from gratis, which specifically means that something costs no money.

example.en: The project uses free and open-source software.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tabla can mean a flat wooden board. The same written plural can also mean tables of information, so the pictured object determines the sense here.

example.en: They bought boards for the floor.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; made of or from (introducing a material)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After an object or an expression such as ser de or estar hecho de, de introduces the material that composes it.

example.en: The door is made of metal.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In cultura popular, popular refers to entertainment, ideas, and references widely shared by the public.

example.en: It is a popular song.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the Buffyverse; the fictional universe of Buffy
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish fandom writing can add -verso to a name to refer to the shared fictional universe around it. This coined term behaves as a masculine noun after el.

example.es: El personaje aparece en el buffyverso.
example.en: The character appears in the Buffyverse.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: usually; tends to (before an action verb)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Suele is the singular present form of soler. It is followed by another verb in its unchanged dictionary form to describe a habitual action.

example.en: Ana usually walks to work.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hecha is the feminine singular form of hecho. With estar hecha de, it describes the material composing a feminine singular thing.

example.es: La caja está hecha de cartón.
example.en: The box is made of cardboard.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Patio can describe an outdoor area beside or enclosed by a house. In a school setting, the same word can mean playground or schoolyard.

example.es: Los niños juegan en el patio de la casa.
example.en: The children play in the yard of the house.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here serie is a continuing television production made up of episodes, rather than a numerical sequence or a general group of things.

example.en: They started a new TV series.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is found or located somewhere?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of encontrarse, then en, then the place.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Encontrarse contains the small matching word se in the dictionary form. In a sentence, both parts match what is located: la tienda se encuentra and las tiendas se encuentran. En introduces the location. This use describes where something is; it does not mean that two people meet each other.

example.es: La biblioteca se encuentra en la plaza.
example.en: The library is located in the square.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you link two items with the meaning ‘both one and the other’?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put tanto before the first item and como before the second item.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The letters X and Y stand for the two parallel items being linked. Each item can itself begin with a preposition such as para, de, or como, so repeated words are possible. The two items should play the same grammatical role.

example.es: Usamos la mesa tanto para comer como para trabajar.
example.en: We use the table both for eating and for working.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to material used for building?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use material de construcción for ‘construction material.’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This established combination uses de to link material to construcción, the activity of building. English places ‘construction’ directly before ‘material,’ while Spanish keeps the nouns joined by de.

example.en: We need durable construction material.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the Spanish name for the instrument called a rain stick?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use palo de lluvia for ‘rain stick.’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A palo de lluvia is a hollow tube containing small pieces that make a rain-like sound when it is tilted. The established name joins palo and lluvia with de.

example.es: Agitó un palo de lluvia durante la canción.
example.en: She shook a rain stick during the song.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say what material something is made from?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of estar, then hecho, hecha, hechos, or hechas to match the thing, then de and the material.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estar changes for the thing and the time: está or estaba, for example. Hecho is the completed-action form of hacer, ‘to make,’ and changes to hecha, hechos, or hechas to match the thing described. De introduces the material; the plus sign in the prompt means that the material comes next.

example.es: La mesa está hecha de metal.
example.en: The table is made of metal.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you state simply what material something is made of?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of ser, then de, then the material.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: English normally says ‘is made of,’ but Spanish can omit a separate word for ‘made’: la taza es de vidrio. Only ser changes for the thing or time; de stays unchanged, and the plus sign in the prompt means that the material comes next.

example.en: The keys are made of metal.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the joke parodies encyclopedia sections that collect every passing reference to a subject in entertainment
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Wikipedia articles have often included ‘In popular culture’ sections listing appearances in films, television, books, and games. The comic applies that format to an extremely ordinary substance and fills it with trivial examples, while the recursive title text imagines the section itself receiving the same treatment.

regions.labelEs: LA MADERA ES UN TEJIDO DURO Y FIBROSO QUE SE ENCUENTRA EN MUCHAS PLANTAS. SE HA USADO DURANTE SIGLOS TANTO COMO COMBUSTIBLE COMO MATERIAL DE CONSTRUCCIÓN PARA...

applications.explanationEn: Tejido names the material first; duro and fibroso follow it as two neutral descriptions joined by y.
Duro and fibroso use masculine singular -o because both describe the masculine singular noun tejido.
Se encuentra is singular because the located material is singular, while en muchas plantas supplies the filled location.
Ha supplies the present helper haber, and usado is usar's completed-action form.
Se leaves the people doing the using unnamed, while ha usado presents that use as completed and relevant to the present.

applications.exampleEs: TANTO COMO COMBUSTIBLE COMO MATERIAL DE CONSTRUCCIÓN
applications.explanationEn: Tanto opens the first role, como combustible, and the second como introduces the parallel role material de construcción.
De links material to construcción to form the established name for material intended for building.

applications.explanationEn: Cultura names the subject first, and popular follows it as the neutral description.
Popular has one singular form for both genders, so it remains popular while describing the feminine singular noun cultura.
